newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's budget blues seen lifting yields.
newsitem.headline: Poland's budget blues seen lifting yields.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to rise at Monday's 1.4 billion zloty T-bill auction as the finance ministry is hard pressed for funds after running out of cash last week, dealers said on Friday.
"Yields should rise on Monday as banks will test for higher levels, knowing that the finance ministry needs cash," said Maciej Ratulowski, dealer at Bank Zachodni SA.
The treasury briefly delayed paying some public sector workers last week, but Finance Minister Marek Belka said that all back payments would be made by June 13.

Dealers said the benchmark 52-week T-bill yield could rise to about 21.55 percent on Monday from last week's 21.45 percent, but that even such an increase does not have to translate into larger demand at the tender.

"The monthly T-bill offer schedule has not been announced, so banks may refrain from placing large bids on Monday because the treasury may hold a bigger tender only a few days later," said Maciek Kwiatkowski, dealer at Societe Generale.
The average yield of the 26-week week T-bill was expected to rise to 21.47 or 21.50 from 21.44 percent on Wednesday.
The shortest 13-week bill yield was seen around 21.00 percent, up from 20.82 percent at last Monday's tender.
On Monday the treasury will offer 900 million zlotys of the benchmark paper, 100 million zlotys of 26-week bills and 400 million of 13-week T-bills.

Dealers said foreigners would refrain from large entry at the tender as Polish interest rates were on hold and the zloty was not expected to appreciate against its basket of five Western currencies in the medium-term.
The zloty may again be doomed to drift sideways against the basket at the central bank-enforced resistance level of 1.5 percent above parity for most of next week, dealers said.

But they said that capital inflows for Bank Handlowy's one billion zloty public offer could buoy the local unit. Handlowy is due to set the price of its IPO on June 17, with capital inflows following until around June 23.

"After ending this week on a weaker note, the zloty should remain idle around 1.5 percent early next week with Handlowy inflows potentially putting the zloty under upward pressure later," said Witold Wozniak, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
Wozniak added however, that if a large part of these capital inflows were done through the post-trade fixing, the effect on the local currency exchange market would be minute.
The zloty was fixed on Friday at 1.46 percent from parity, slightly lower than last week's close at 1.48 percent.
It was at 3.2400 to the dollar and at 1.8725 to the mark, against last week's 3.2370 and 1.8640.

On the money market one-day rates should next week remain around the central bank's main 14-day drainage rate of 22.15 percent as banks have free cash on their hands, unless the central bank heavily drained the market, dealers said.
